31:20.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَسۡبَغَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعَمَهُۥ ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَبَاطِنَةࣰۗ وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا هُدࣰ ى وَلَا كِتَٰبࣲ مُّنِيرࣲ‏
31:20.en: See ye not how Allah hath made serviceable unto you whatsoever is in the skies and whatsoever is in the earth and hath loaded you with His favours both without and within? Yet of mankind is he who disputeth concerning Allah, without knowledge or guidance or a scripture giving light

31:21.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
31:21.en: And if it be said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: Nay, but we follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though the devil were inviting them unto the doom of flame

31:22.ar: ۞وَمَن يُسۡلِمۡ وَجۡهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:22.en: Whosoever surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good, he verily hath grasped the firm hand-hold. Unto Allah belongeth the sequel of all things

31:23.ar: وَمَن كَفَرَ فَلَا يَحۡزُنكَ كُفۡرُهُۥٓۚ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُهُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
31:23.en: And whosoever disbelieveth, let not his disbelief afflict thee (O Muhammad). Unto Us is their return, and We shall tell them what they did. Lo! Allah is Aware of what is in the breasts (of men)

31:24.ar: نُمَتِّعُهُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ نَضۡطَرُّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
31:24.en: We give them comfort for a little, and then We drive them to a heavy doom

45:13.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا مِّنۡهُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
45:13.en: And hath made of service unto you whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; it is all from Him. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who reflect

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ
14:33.en: And maketh the sun and the moon, constant in their courses, to be of service unto you, and hath made of service unto you the night and the day

14:34.ar: وَءَاتَىٰكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُۚ وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَظَلُومࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
14:34.en: And He giveth you of all ye ask of Him, and if ye would count the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! man is verily a wrong-doer, an ingrate

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise

2:8.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:8.en: And of mankind are some who say: We believe in Allah and the Last Day, when they believe not

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And among mankind is he who worshippeth Allah upon a narrow marge so that if good befalleth him he is content therewith, but if a trial befalleth him, he falleth away utterly. He loseth both the world and the Hereafter. That is the sheer loss

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent and had no guidance

5:104.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ قَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
5:104.en: And when it is said unto them: Come unto that which Allah hath revealed and unto the messenger, they say: Enough for us is that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers had no knowledge whatsoever, and no guidance

103:2.en: Lo! man is a state of loss

103:3.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ
103:3.en: Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance

4:46.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعࣲ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنࣰ ا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
4:46.en: Some of those who are Jews change words from their context and say: "We hear and disobey; hear thou as one who heareth not" and "Listen to us!" distorting with their tongues and slandering religion. If they had said: "We hear and we obey: hear thou, and look at us" it had been better for them, and more upright. But Allah hath cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do

31:2.en: These are revelations of the wise Scripture

31:3.en: A guidance and a mercy for the good

4EG55pE7Ey4.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Luqman (Verses 20-24)
4EG55pE7Ey4.one_line: The commentary after Luqman's counsel: a creation made subservient to us, gratitude between generations, and why following forefathers blindly is rejected.
4EG55pE7Ey4.summary: After explaining how surahs are built, he reads verses 20 to 24 as Allah's commentary on Luqman's counsel. The plural address shows that the relationship between generations, like any relationship, works only when both sides make an effort. Everything in the heavens and earth has been made subservient to humans, which makes them responsible for its care and use, and blessings cover people outwardly and inwardly. Gratitude is the lens through which elders and children should see one another: as blessings rather than burdens; he explains his own patience with youth by not knowing which of them Allah will use for great things. Placed right after a wise father's counsel, the verse condemning those who follow their forefathers shows that the young must neither worship nor dismiss the previous generation. Submission belongs to Allah alone; even scholars and companions erred, and Islam survived by balancing inherited and new. Parenting methods from the home countries are a means to righteousness and success, not a sacred end. Whoever submits to Allah while doing excellent work, setting aside pride, holds the firmest handhold. As for those who will not listen, their reckoning is with Allah; the believer's job is to speak, call and model.

outline.heading: Recap: the surah builds the bond between generations
outline.gist: The first nineteen verses centre on Luqman's counsel; the surah's aim is the relationship between parents and children.

outline.heading: How surahs are structured
outline.gist: Some have introduction, body and conclusion; some are sections; some build to a pivotal verse followed by commentary.

outline.heading: Short surahs as single pills of medicine
outline.gist: The last juz' presents one idea quickly; Luqman, though short, has an introduction, pivotal verses and commentary.

outline.heading: Recitation of the commentary verses
outline.gist: Recitation of the verses on subjugated creation, those who dispute about Allah, and following forefathers.

outline.heading: Do you not all see: both sides must try
outline.gist: The plural address speaks to both parent and child; any marriage, friendship or work relationship fails if one side makes no effort.

outline.heading: Subjugation: creation exists for you
outline.gist: Taskhir differs from creation: the planet was made with you as its purpose.

outline.heading: What is subjugated to you is your responsibility
outline.gist: You must protect, care for and use well what serves you, as far as you are able.

outline.heading: Isbagh: a complete covering
outline.gist: The word as in completing wudu in hardship; doing a hard command fully brings great reward.

outline.heading: Blessings outward and inward lead to gratitude
outline.gist: A planet with everything needed, plus guidance and intellect; the verse returns to Luqman's first lesson of gratitude.

outline.heading: Gratitude for each other across generations
outline.gist: Elderly parents seen as a burden and children blamed for lost freedom ruin relationships; their mere presence is a blessing despite the hardship.

outline.heading: A grateful mind sees elders and youth differently
outline.gist: The verse is comprehensive in gratitude; you can see the same person through twenty eyes and must choose gratitude.

outline.heading: Why he is patient with young people
outline.gist: He never knows which child may become a Salahuddin, so he sees potential where others see noise and bad manners.

outline.heading: Those who dispute about Allah without knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran uses 'among people' to expose ignorant acts without naming people; they argue about the One who gave them everything.

outline.heading: Be unlike the ungrateful
outline.gist: If people speak ill even of Allah, expect criticism yourself; they lack knowledge, guidance and an illuminating book, so be grateful instead.

outline.heading: Following forefathers right after a wise father
outline.gist: Why the verse on blind ancestral following comes directly after Luqman's counsel.

outline.heading: The Quran does not ask for blind acceptance
outline.gist: The Quran's quarrel is with blind following; the placement is deliberate, warning against misreading Luqman's story.

outline.heading: Neither sanctify nor dismiss the elders
outline.gist: No one is all right or all wrong; only the eye of gratitude lets you separate what benefits from what harms.

outline.heading: Quraysh and their fathers
outline.gist: The Prophet spent twenty years arguing that respected fathers can still be wrong; some replied they would follow them to hell.

outline.heading: Knowledge cannot grow inside our predecessors' cloaks
outline.gist: Elders cannot decide every detail of their children's lives; humanity would not advance otherwise.

outline.heading: The religion of your father Ibrahim
outline.gist: If it is about ancestors, go back to Ibrahim and Adam; yet his call was to Allah, not to ancestry.

outline.heading: Balance: you need someone who walked the road
outline.gist: Neither take all nor reject all; whoever has no elder should find one who has walked the path before you.

outline.heading: Mutual counsel is two-way
outline.gist: Al-Asr: counsel among believers is mutual; even Allah responds to His servants' prayers and questions.

outline.heading: We hear and disobey versus we hear and obey
outline.gist: Those who twisted words with their prophets, against the right way: hear and obey, then ask for time.

outline.heading: Submit to no one but Allah
outline.gist: No believer has a choice once Allah and His Messenger decide; complete submission belongs to Allah alone.

outline.heading: Verify that it is really the Prophet's meaning
outline.gist: Check that a preacher quoting the Prophet conveys his actual intent and is not bending it for an agenda.

outline.heading: Scholars and companions were not infallible
outline.gist: Discovering that a great figure erred should not shake faith; they were human and watched constantly.

outline.heading: Islam survived by balancing old and new
outline.gist: What is new today is old in twenty years; Quraysh rejected the Prophet's message as new.

outline.heading: Recitation: whoever submits his face to Allah
outline.gist: Recitation of the verses on submission, the firm handhold and those who disbelieve.

outline.heading: Islam means surrendering your own will
outline.gist: Submitting yourself as one surrenders to police: replacing your choice with Allah's.

outline.heading: Do not surrender yourself to your parents
outline.gist: Parents may command what contradicts Allah or causes harm; he received objections after saying Luqman did not demand birr.

outline.heading: Parenting methods from the home countries
outline.gist: Methods used where we grew up may not all work in this country; what matters is the purpose.

outline.heading: Upbringing is a means, not the goal
outline.gist: The goal is a righteous, successful child; keep the methods that worked on you and drop those that did not or no longer will.

outline.heading: Submitting the face: setting pride aside
outline.gist: The face stands for the self; elders' and youths' pride toward each other blocks the relationship.

outline.heading: While doing excellent work
outline.gist: Echoing the surah's opening on the muhsinin: the aim is achieving the good, not showing off or being proven right.

outline.heading: The firmest handhold
outline.gist: Al-'urwah al-wuthqa holds under any weight, unlike attractive human ideas that collapse under criticism.

outline.heading: Do not grieve over those who disbelieve
outline.gist: Some, old or young, will never listen; Allah will inform them of their error on the Day they return.

outline.heading: He knows what is in the breasts; brief enjoyment
outline.gist: Allah exposes even intentions; a lifetime of power is little before being compelled to a harsh punishment.

outline.heading: Your task is to call, not to judge
outline.gist: Do not take on Allah's role of punishing or reckoning; talk, invite and be an example.
